mainTopic: Where do we learn to follow a majority we cannot see (רובא דליתא קמן)? A series of proofs from animals that are never checked for being טריפה
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: a row of men reports to the כהן that a נגע in a house has stayed the same. That is how רב אחא בר יעקב explains the ברייתא, so for him it is no proof that we rely on חזקה. Then a new topic begins: where do we learn to follow the majority (זיל בתר רובא)? The גמרא is surprised at first, since the פסוק ״אחרי רבים להטות״ says it outright. It explains that a majority we can see and count, like nine shops or the votes of a סנהדרין, is clearly covered. The real question is about a majority we cannot see, like assuming a קטן and קטנה will grow up normally. A series of sages then try to prove it from animals that the תורה says are used without being checked inside, so they might be טריפה. The proofs come from the head of an עולה, the bones of the קרבן פסח, and the אליה of a שלמים, and each one is rejected because the animal could be checked after all. More proofs follow from the עגלה ערופה and the פרה אדומה, each defended against the objection that a טריפה would not matter. The amud ends in the middle of a new proof from the two goats of יום כיפור, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A row of men passes word about the mark to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion. The כהן knows the נגע did not change as he walked out, because a line of people passes the word along that it stayed the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where a row of men stands between the house and the כהן, and each one says: it is still the same as it was.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last answer in the earlier discussion about נגעי בתים. רב אחא בר יעקב explains the ברייתא that lets the כהן declare the quarantine even from inside his own house: a line of men passes word to him that the mark has not changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב held that the כהן walks out backward, watching the mark, so the מצורע house is no proof for חזקה. The ברייתא seemed to go against him, since it allows the quarantine even from the כהן's own house, where he cannot see the mark. He answers that a row of men stands from the house to the כהן, and each one tells the next that the mark is the same (Rashi). So the כהן knows directly, and no חזקה is needed here.

keyTerms.meaning: A row (line) of men
It stands as it stood, meaning it has not changed
A presumption that something stays the way it was

steps.whatToRemember: This line ends the discussion of חזקה. The next line starts a new topic, רובא.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new discussion. It is the end of a back-and-forth from the previous part of the דף, about the כהן leaving a house that has a נגע.

phrases.english: For example, where a row of men stands
phrases.notes: The men stand in a line from the house with the נגע to wherever the כהן is standing.

phrases.english: and they say: as it stood, it stands.
phrases.notes: Each man tells the next one that the mark has stayed the same size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אחא בר יעקב's answer to the ברייתא quoted just before this section, which allows the quarantine even from inside the כהן's own house.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical way the facts can be known (people report the mark's state)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows the quarantine even when the כהן cannot see the mark, which seems to prove we rely on חזקה, against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.terutzMaskana: A row of men tells the כהן the mark stayed the same, so he knows directly, and the ברייתא does not prove we rely on חזקה.

steps.title: Where do we learn to follow the majority?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. The גמרא asks where the rule of following the majority comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this thing the רבנן said: go after the majority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion. It asks for the source of the well-known rule that we follow the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after dealing with חזקה, the גמרא turns to the second big tool for deciding a doubt, which is רובא. The question as asked sounds like a simple request for a source. The next steps show that the question is more pointed than it first looks.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is this matter known? (a request for a source)
Go after the majority
Majority

phrases.english: From where is this matter
that the Rabbis said: go after the majority?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of חזקה to the related topic of רובא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for following the majority.

steps.title: Surprise: a פסוק says it outright
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question, because the תורה clearly says ״אחרי רבים להטות״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know it?! It is written: ״after the majority to incline.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reacts with surprise. Why ask for a source when a פסוק openly says to follow the majority?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is also a kind of push-back. If the source is so obvious, the original question must have meant something else. That sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains what is really being asked.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?
Lean after the majority (a פסוק about how judges decide)

phrases.english: From where do we know it?!
As it is written: "After the majority to incline."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2 with an obvious פסוק, which hints that the question must mean something deeper.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״אחרי רבים להטות״ teaches that we follow the majority.

steps.title: A majority we can see is not the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a majority in front of us, like nine kosher shops out of ten or the votes of a סנהדרין, is clearly covered by the פסוק. That is not what was being asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: A majority that is in front of us, such as nine shops, and the סנהדרין, we are not asking about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own surprise. It agrees that a majority we can see and count needs no further proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about judges voting, where the majority is right there and can be counted. Other cases where the majority is countable, like a piece of meat found near nine kosher shops and one non-kosher shop, are just as clear. So the question in step 2 must be about some other kind of majority.

keyTerms.meaning: A majority that is in front of us, one we can see and count
Nine shops (the case of meat found near shops, most of them kosher)
The court of judges, which decides by majority vote
We do not have a question about it

phrases.english: A majority that is in front of us,
such as nine shops, and the Sanhedrin –
phrases.notes: Nine shops sell kosher meat and one does not, so meat found nearby is assumed to come from the majority.

phrases.english: we are not asking about that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the obvious פסוק from step 3 does not end the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows what the question is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question in step 2 seemed silly, since a פסוק openly says to follow the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק clearly covers a countable majority, so the question must be about a different kind.

steps.title: The real question: a majority we cannot see
steps.stepSummary: The real question is about a majority that is not in front of us, like assuming a קטן and קטנה will grow up normally. Where do we learn to follow that kind of majority?
steps.simpleTranslation: What we are asking about is a majority that is not in front of us, such as a minor boy and a minor girl. From where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states its real question. It wants a source for relying on a majority we cannot see or count, like what happens to most children as they grow up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the majority is just a general fact about how most people turn out. It is not a group we can count in front of us. We rely on it anyway, for example by letting a קטן and קטנה marry in יבום without worrying that one of them will never develop. Since the פסוק about judges does not clearly cover this, the גמרא needs a new source, which it will look for next.

keyTerms.meaning: A majority that is not in front of us, a general fact about how most cases turn out
A minor boy and a minor girl (here, in a case of יבום)
When we do have a question, this is what it is about

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of רובא: one in front of us (רובא דאיתא קמן), learned clearly from ״אחרי רבים״, and one not in front of us (רובא דליתא קמן), which still needs a source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between two kinds of majority shows up all over the תלמוד. The search for a source for the unseen kind is the main topic of the discussion that follows.

phrases.english: When we do ask,
it is about a majority that is not in front of us,
such as a minor boy and a minor girl. From where do we know it?
phrases.notes: We assume they will develop normally like most people, even though we cannot check that yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out the countable majority in step 4, this states the real question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in the תורה for following a majority that is not in front of us (רובא דליתא קמן).

steps.title: Proof from the head of a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר proves we follow an unseen majority. The head of an עולה is offered whole and unchecked, so we must be assuming that most animals are not טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said (a memory aid for the names: זמן שבח מכנש): We learn it from the head of an עולה. The פסוק says "and he shall cut it into its pieces." That means you cut the animal into its pieces, but you do not cut those pieces into smaller pieces. So the head is never opened. Shouldn't we worry that the brain membrane was pierced, which would make the animal a טריפה? We must not worry about this only because we say: follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question from Step 5. He shows a case where the תורה itself lets us offer an animal without checking it, so we must be relying on the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pierced brain membrane makes an animal a טריפה, and a טריפה cannot be a קרבן. The head of an עולה stays whole, so its membrane is never examined. Since the תורה still lets us offer it, the reason must be that most animals are healthy. That majority is not in front of us, and this is exactly the kind of majority Step 5 asked about.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, here made of letters standing for the names of the sages who will answer
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Pieces. The animal is cut into its main pieces, and those are not cut further
The membrane that covers the brain. If it is pierced, the animal is a טריפה
An animal with a fatal defect. It is forbidden to eat and unfit to be a קרבן
Go after the majority

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said
(a mnemonic: Zaman Shevach Mechanesh):
phrases.notes: Each letter hints at one of the sages who will answer this question in the coming lines.

phrases.english: It is derived from the head of a burnt offering,
as the verse says: "And he shall cut it into its pieces,"
it into its pieces, but not its pieces into more pieces,
phrases.notes: The head counts as one of the pieces, so it stays whole and is never opened.

phrases.aramaic: וְנֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ?
phrases.english: so let us worry that perhaps the brain membrane was pierced?
Rather, is it not because we say:
go after the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first source to answer the question raised in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow a majority that is not in front of us
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that the head of an עולה is not cut into pieces (ויקרא 1:6), so its brain membrane is never checked

steps.title: Maybe the head is split and checked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps the head is split open and checked, but its two halves are left joined, so it is not truly cut into pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe he splits the head open and checks it. And if you object that the head may not be cut into pieces, that rule applies only when you cut it completely apart. When the two halves stay joined, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר's proof. It suggests that the head of the עולה can be checked after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof worked only if the head could never be checked. The גמרא suggests splitting the head open while keeping the halves attached. That is not counted as cutting a piece into pieces. If the membrane can be checked this way, we are relying on the check and not on the majority, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? A standard opening for rejecting a proof
Perhaps
Splits open
Stays joined or attached

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject the idea of following an unseen majority. It only says this particular case does not prove it.

phrases.english: From where do you know?
Perhaps he splits it open and checks it,
and if you object because of "it into its pieces"
and not its pieces into more pieces,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּחָתֵיךְ לֵיהּ לִגְמָרֵי,
phrases.english: that applies only where he cuts it completely apart,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלַיִיף לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but where it stays joined, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא דְּפָלֵי לֵיהּ וּבָדֵק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the head of the עולה, not the principle itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The head can be split and checked while the halves stay joined, so no unseen majority is needed

steps.title: Proof from the bones of the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא brings a new proof. No bone of the קרבן פסח may be broken, so its brain can never be checked, and we must be relying on the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא said: We learn it from the rule about breaking a bone of the קרבן פסח. The תורה says "you shall not break a bone of it." So shouldn't we worry that the brain membrane was pierced? We must not worry about this only because we say: follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: A new sage brings a different proof, chosen so that the objection from Step 7 cannot touch it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the עולה, the head could still be split and checked. With the קרבן פסח, no bone may be broken at all, so the skull can never be opened to check the membrane. Since the קרבן פסח is still offered and eaten, we must be relying on the majority of animals not being טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Passover offering
Breaking a bone, which is forbidden with the קרבן פסח
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: מר בריה דרבינא picked the קרבן פסח because its bones may never be broken, which seems to block the objection that knocked down the עולה proof in step 7. The next step shows that this proof is also rejected.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said:
It is derived from breaking a bone in the Passover offering,
as the Merciful One said: "And you shall not break a bone of it,"

phrases.aramaic: וְנֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ?
phrases.english: so let us worry that perhaps the brain membrane was pierced?
Rather, is it not because we say:
go after the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from Step 6 with one that avoids the objection in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow a majority that is not in front of us
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ban on breaking a bone of the קרבן פסח (שמות 12:46), so its brain membrane can never be checked

steps.title: The brain of the פסח could be checked by burning through the skull
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects מר בריה דרבינא's proof. Perhaps a coal is placed on the head of the פסח to burn a hole in the skull and check the brain. A ברייתא teaches that burning a bone is not the forbidden act of breaking a bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe he puts a hot coal on the head, burns through it, and checks the brain. As a ברייתא teaches: someone who cuts the sinews or burns the bones of the פסח does not break the rule against breaking a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the קרבן פסח. It shows there is a way to check the brain without breaking any bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 8 assumed the brain of the פסח could never be checked, because no bone may be broken. The גמרא answers that burning a hole is not 'breaking', and a ברייתא backs this up. So the brain could be checked after all, and we do not need to be relying on the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: A burning coal
Burns or roasts
Sinews
Breaking a bone, which is forbidden with the קרבן פסח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is allowing people to break the bone. It is saying that burning through a bone is a different act, and it does not count as 'breaking' at all.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps he places a coal on it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the head of the קרבן פסח from the last step.

phrases.english: and burns through it, and checks it,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: one who cuts the sinews
or burns the bones
has not violated the rule against breaking a bone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the brain of the קרבן פסח given in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. The underlying rule of following an unseen majority is not challenged.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the brain cannot be checked without breaking a bone. In fact it can be checked by burning through the skull, which is not considered breaking.

steps.title: Proof from the tail of a שלמים, which must be offered whole
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves we follow an unseen majority from the אליה (fat tail), which the תורה says must be offered whole. The spinal cord runs through it and could have been torn, yet it is not checked. That means we are relying on the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We learn it from the fat tail, since the תורה says, 'its fat, the whole tail.' We should worry that the spinal cord inside it was torn. So the reason we do not worry must be that we say: follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: A new proof is offered. The tail of a קרבן שלמים must stay whole, so no one can open it to check the spinal cord inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the spinal cord is torn, the animal is a טריפה and cannot be brought as a קרבן. Since the תורה requires the tail to be offered whole and unchecked, it must be assuming the animal is fine, just like most animals are. That is following a majority that is not in front of us.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat tail of a sheep
Whole, complete
The spinal cord
Go after the majority

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same type of proof as רבי אלעזר's proof from the head of the עולה. It looks for a body part that the תורה requires to stay intact, so it could never have been checked.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אָתְיָא מֵאַלְיָה,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: it is learned from the tail,
since the Merciful One said:
'Its fat, the tail whole,'
so let us worry that perhaps the spinal cord was torn?
Rather, is it not because we say:
go after the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אָתְיָא מֵאַלְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the פסח was rejected in step 9, a new source is offered.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow a majority that is not in front of us (most animals are not טריפה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק requiring the אליה of a שלמים to be offered whole, ויקרא 3:9.

steps.title: The tail is cut at a spot where a torn spinal cord matters
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק expects someone to object that the tail is cut below the part of the spine that matters. He answers from the פסוק: the tail is removed 'opposite the עצה', near the kidneys. That is a spot where a torn spinal cord does make the animal a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that he cuts it off lower down, the תורה said 'opposite the עצה', meaning the place where the kidneys 'give advice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The proof is being defended against an expected objection. The objection would be that the tail is cut low enough that the spinal cord there does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tail were cut far down, a tear there would not make the animal a טריפה, and the proof would fall apart. The פסוק places the cut near the kidneys, high enough that the spinal cord there does count. So the proof stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (this brings up a possible objection)
From below
The rump bone near the base of the spine
Kidneys

phrases.english: And if you will say that he cuts it off from below,
phrases.notes: He means below the part of the spine where a tear would make it a טריפה.

phrases.english: the Merciful One said 'opposite the עצה,'
the place where the kidneys give advice.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: עצה sounds like 'advice', and the kidneys were seen as advisers. It points to the area near the kidneys.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the proof from step 10 against an expected objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Anticipated objection answered from the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the tail is cut below the critical part of the spine, so no check would be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק places the cut opposite the עצה, near the kidneys, where a torn spinal cord does make the animal a טריפה.

steps.title: The tail could be split and checked while staying joined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the tail. Perhaps the tail is opened and checked. 'Whole' only forbids cutting it all the way apart, and leaving the halves joined is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe he opens it up and checks it. And if you object because it must be 'whole', that is only when he cuts it all the way through. But if the halves stay joined, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof. It shows the tail could be checked without breaking the rule that it must be whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that 'whole' means the tail can never be opened. The גמרא says 'whole' only means it may not be cut into separate pieces. A slit that leaves the halves joined still counts as whole, so the tail could be checked, and the proof does not show we rely on the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Opened, split open
These words apply (only) to...
Completely
Joined, still attached
We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: Both the head of the עולה (step 7) and the tail of the שלמים are rejected for the same reason: something can be split open and checked while still counting as 'whole', as long as the parts stay joined.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps he opens it and checks it,
and if you object because of 'whole',
that applies only where he cuts it completely,
but where it stays joined,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא דְּפָתַח לַהּ וּבָדֵיק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the tail in steps 10 and 11, using the same reasoning as the rejection in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the אליה. The search for a source continues.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'whole' forbids any opening. In fact it only forbids cutting the tail completely apart, so the tail could be opened and checked.

steps.title: Proof from the heifer whose neck is broken
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי proves we follow the majority from the עגלה ערופה. It must remain whole, so it can never be checked for being a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת son of רב אידי said: We learn it from the עגלה ערופה. The תורה calls it 'the broken-necked one,' so it must stay whole. But maybe it is a טריפה! It must be that we follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא brings another proof that we rely on the majority of animals being healthy. He uses the עגלה ערופה, an animal whose insides are never checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the heifer as 'broken-necked' at the time of the hand-washing. That shows its only change should be the broken neck, and it is not cut open. Since nobody checks it for being a טריפה, we must be relying on the majority of animals, which are not טריפות.

keyTerms.meaning: The heifer whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
Whole, not cut open
An animal with a fatal defect that makes it unfit
Let us worry about it
Go after the majority

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said:
It is learned from the heifer whose neck is broken,
as the Merciful One said: "whose neck was broken" —
it should be while it is whole,
but let us worry that perhaps it is a tereifa!
Rather, is it not because we say:
Go after the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר: אָתְיָא מֵעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the אליה was rejected in Step 12, a new source is offered.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow an unseen majority and assume an animal is not a טריפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'העֲרוּפָה', which teaches that the עגלה ערופה must remain whole and cannot be checked

steps.title: A tereifa would matter for this heifer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expects someone to object that it makes no difference if the עגלה ערופה is a טריפה. It answers with דבי רבי ינאי: the heifer brings כפרה like קדשים, so a טריפה would be unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: what difference does it make if it is a טריפה? But the school of רבי ינאי said that atonement is written about it, like sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא protects the proof from a likely objection. Someone might say a טריפה would not matter here, since the heifer is not eaten or offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טריפה were fine for the עגלה ערופה, then not checking it would prove nothing. דבי רבי ינאי point out that the תורה uses the word כפרה about it, so it is treated like קדשים. Like קדשים, a טריפה is unfit, so the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (opens an expected objection)
What difference does it make?
Atonement
Sacrifices, holy offerings

phrases.english: And if you would say: what difference does it make,
but the school of Rabbi Yannai said:
atonement is written regarding it, like sacrifices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the proof from Step 13 against an expected objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Blocks an expected objection by showing that a טריפה would truly be unfit here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the עגלה ערופה is not eaten or offered, maybe a טריפה would not matter, so the proof would fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עגלה ערופה brings כפרה like קדשים, so a טריפה is unfit, and the proof holds.

steps.title: Proof from the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא proves we follow the majority from the פרה אדומה. Its burning must be done while it is whole, just like its slaughter, so it is never checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: We learn it from the פרה אדומה. The תורה says 'he shall slaughter… and he shall burn.' Just as it is slaughtered whole, so too it is burned whole. But maybe it is a טריפה! It must be that we follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא brings a parallel proof, this time from the פרה אדומה. Its insides are never checked either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה puts slaughtering and burning side by side. So just as the slaughter is done while the animal is whole, the burning must also be done while it is whole, without opening it. Since it is never checked for being a טריפה, we must be relying on the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, burned to make ashes for purification
Slaughter
Burning
Just as… so too… (comparing two things)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
It is learned from the red heifer,
as the Merciful One said: "And he shall slaughter… and he shall burn,"
just as its slaughter is while it is whole,
so too its burning is while it is whole,
but let us worry that perhaps it is a tereifa!
Rather, is it not because we say:
Go after the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא אָמַר: אָתְיָא מִפָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a parallel proof built the same way as Step 13, using a different animal.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow an unseen majority and assume an animal is not a טריפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'וְשָׁחַט… וְשָׂרַף', which compares the burning to the slaughter, so the פרה אדומה is burned whole

steps.title: The red heifer is called a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expects the same objection, that a טריפה makes no difference for the פרה אדומה. It answers that the תורה calls it a חטאת, so a טריפה would be unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: what difference does it make if it is a טריפה? The Merciful One called it a 'חטאת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the same expected objection it answered in Step 14, now for the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טריפה were fine for the פרה אדומה, not checking it would prove nothing. But the תורה calls it a חטאת, like a sin offering, and a טריפה is unfit for that. So the פרה אדומה must not be a טריפה, and the proof from the majority stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering. Here it is the name the תורה gives the פרה אדומה.
Called it
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: Two animals that must stay whole, the עגלה ערופה and the פרה אדומה, can never be checked inside. Yet a טריפה would be unfit for both, because one brings כפרה like קדשים and the other is called a חטאת. So they show that we rely on the majority of animals not being טריפות.

phrases.english: And if you would say: what difference does it make?
The Merciful One called it a "sin offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, מַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? ״חַטָּאת״ קַרְיַיהּ רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the proof from Step 15, the same way Step 14 defended Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Blocks an expected objection by showing that a טריפה would truly be unfit here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פרה אדומה is not eaten or offered on the מזבח, maybe a טריפה would not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה calls it a חטאת, so like a sin offering it cannot be a טריפה, and the proof holds.

steps.title: A proof from the two goats of יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says we learn that we follow the majority from the שעיר המשתלח. The פסוק says 'the two goats,' which teaches that both must be equal. The גמרא then begins to raise a worry: what if one of them is a טריפה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: We learn it from the goat that is sent away (the שעיר המשתלח). The תורה says, 'And he shall take the two goats,' which teaches that the two goats must be equal. But we should be concerned...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב brings a sixth proof that we rely on the majority, this time from the two goats of יום כיפור. The last word starts a worry that the גמרא finishes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires the two goats to be the same as each other. The worry being set up is that one goat might be a טריפה, which would break the rule that they must be equal. Since we go ahead anyway without checking, we must be relying on the majority of animals not being טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור
It comes from / it is learned from
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Equal, the same as each other
But let us be concerned, a question that raises a worry

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not finished here. The word וליחוש only opens the worry ('what if one is a טריפה?'), and the גמרא finishes that thought right after this line.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
It is learned from the goat that is sent away,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule that we follow the majority without checking, which the גמרא has been trying to prove.

phrases.english: for the Merciful One says:
"And he shall take the two goats,"
meaning that the two of them should be equal,
but let us be concerned

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: אָתְיָא מִשָּׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another proof to the list, after the עגלה ערופה (Step 13) and the פרה אדומה (Steps 15-16).
steps.raayaObject: That we follow the majority and assume an animal is not a טריפה without checking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule from 'שני השעירים' (ויקרא 16:7) that the two goats of יום כיפור must be equal. The proof only works if we assume, based on the majority, that neither goat is a טריפה.
